chapter: Cab Calloway, Haiti and Sarah Vaughan
title: Lost records and meeting Issa El Saieh again at Montreux
summary: Budd's stored records mildewed, and in 1971 he runs into El Saieh and his son at Montreux.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You know, when I moved from where I lived in Jamaica, and all that stuff my wife put in the garage because I was away, and it all mildewed and spoiled.
But, you know, I can get ahold of those records.

Well, he's a big art dealer. He travels all over the world. In fact, I heard somebody saying, Budd Johnson, Budd Johnson, and I looked around. He was runnin' down the street. We were in Montreux, Switzerland, in '71. He had his son there, whom I knew from a baby, and he had his son there, he said, in the hotel business. He said, no, he said, you can talk about all this education and degrees you want. Learned my son the hotel business. I'm going to build him a hotel, and then let him run it, and he can make his own money, be his own boss, and he can probably take care of his old man in his old age.
